title: Finite-size scaling analysis of three dimensional Z(2) and O(2) spin models with non-vanishing symmetry breaking parameter
authors: Jishnu Goswami, Frithjof Karsch, Sabarnya Mitra
abstract: We present results from a detailed finite-size scaling analysis of the $3$-$d$, $Z(2)$ and $O(2)$ spin models in an external field $H$. Using high statistics Monte Carlo data, we obtain the leading finite-size scaling correction to the infinite volume scaling functions. We show that these corrections are proportional to $\widetilde{z}_L^2=1/(H L^{3/(1+1/δ))})^{2}$. This provides the parametric form for finite-size corrections to bulk thermodynamic observables as well as the pseudo-critical temperatures determined at non-vanishing $H$. In particular, it allows to eliminate systematic errors in the analysis of the chiral phase transition temperature in (2+1)-flavor QCD, that arose from the previously not well-controlled ansatz for infinite volume extrapolations. We also establish the validity range of this leading order correction and point out that there are significant differences between the $3$-$d$, $O(2)$ and $Z(2)$ universality classes.
summary: This work performs a detailed finite-size scaling analysis on 3D Z(2) and O(2) spin models in an external field. By determining the leading finite-size correction term, the authors provide a robust method to eliminate systematic errors in calculating critical parameters. This methodology is particularly valuable for studying quantum phase transitions, such as those found in QCD.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine the leading finite-size scaling corrections to universal functions for 3D Z(2) and O(2) spin models when an external symmetry breaking field is present.
main_result:
The leading finite-size correction is found to be proportional to $e_{z_L}^2 \sim 1/(H L^{1/
u_c})^2$, allowing for the precise elimination of systematic errors in critical temperature determinations, such as in (2+1)-flavor QCD.
method: The study employs detailed finite-size scaling (FSS) analysis using high statistics Monte Carlo simulations, fitting scaled observables to scaling ansatze derived from the Renormalization Group approach.
model_or_system: The physical system is the 3-dimensional Z(2) and O(2) spin models, studied under the influence of a non-vanishing external magnetic field H. The analysis uses concepts from lattice field theory and critical phenomena.
key_observables: The primary observables are the singular parts of thermodynamic quantities, including the order parameter (M) and susceptibility ($\chi_M$), analyzed via scaling functions $f_{\chi}(z, z_L)$ and $f_G(z, z_L)$.
important_parameters:
Key parameters include the external field H, lattice size L, and the scaling variable $e_{z_L} = 1/(H L^{1/
u_c})$. Critical exponents ($\delta,  eta, 
u_c$) are also determined.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the leading order finite-size correction is controlled by the parameter $e_{z_L}^2$, and it compares results across different scaling variables to estimate systematic uncertainties.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows scaled observables ($\chi_M/M$, etc.) plotted against $e_{z_L}$ and $e_{z_L}^2$ for both Z(2) and O(2) models. Figure 6 compares the free energy density $f_G$ for both models at zero and non-zero fields. Figure 7 shows the ratio $H\chi M/M$ versus the coupling $z$ for the Z(2) model.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the scaling functions for the spin models, first establishing the appropriate scaling variable ($e_{z_L}^2$), then fitting data to extract leading and next-to-leading order coefficients, and finally applying these results to fix systematic errors in physical observables like the chiral transition temperature.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics models, the rigorous application of finite-size scaling techniques and the connection to QCD phase transitions provide valuable methodological insights applicable to quantum critical points in many-body quantum systems.
